messages.text:
The comparison caught two useful fidelity issues: Windows text mode was turning `\n` into `\r\n`, and my `ls` included `.git` where Nushell’s default listing does not.

Those are straightforward fixes; I’m also making `compile.sh` detect Windows through Python so it reliably leaves the `.cmd` entrypoint.

#!/usr/bin/env sh
set -eu
rm -f executable executable.exe executable.bat executable.js executable.jar
if command -v python >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  PY=python
else
  PY=python3
fi
"$PY" -m py_compile nushell_port.py executable.py
if [ "${OS:-}" = "Windows_NT" ]; then
  cat > executable.cmd <<'EOF'
@echo off
python "%~dp0executable.py" %*
EOF
else
  cp executable.py executable
  chmod +x executable
fi

import subprocess, pathlib
nu=pathlib.Path('REFERENCE_BINARY.txt').read_text().strip(); port=['python','executable.py']
cmds=['1 + 2','1 + 2 * 3','(1 + 2) * 3','[1 2 3] | math sum','[1 2 3] | length','{a: 1, b: test} | to json','\"a,b\\\\n1,2\" | from csv | to json','[{a: 1 b: 2} {a: 3 b: 4}] | to csv','\"hello\" | str upcase','\"HELLO\" | str downcase','\" hello \" | str trim','\"abc\" | str contains b','\"abc\" | str replace b X','pwd','ls | length','open REFERENCE_BINARY.txt | str trim','[1 2 3] | first','[1 2 3] | last','[1 2 3] | get 1','3 < 4','10 / 4','10 // 4','10 mod 4','2 ** 3']
fail=0
for c in cmds:
 r=subprocess.run([nu,'--no-config-file','-c',c],capture_output=True)
 p=subprocess.run(port+['--no-config-file','-c',c],capture_output=True)
 ok=(r.returncode==p.returncode and r.stdout==p.stdout and r.stderr==p.stderr)
 print(('OK ' if ok else 'BAD'), c)
 if not ok:
  fail+=1; print(' ref',r.returncode,repr(r.stdout.decode('utf-8','replace')),repr(r.stderr.decode('utf-8','replace')[:200])); print(' got',p.returncode,repr(p.stdout.decode('utf-8','replace')),repr(p.stderr.decode('utf-8','replace')[:200]))
print('fail', fail)
'@ | python -"
